title: Paying Engineers like Salespeople – Arman Hezarkhani, Tenex
talk_summary: A consultancy pays engineers a base salary plus a per-story-point bonus, mirroring sales commissions, to incentivize fast, high-quality delivery in an AI-assisted workflow. Guardrails are strategist-owned scoping, multi-round internal QA plus client acceptance per ticket, and very selective hiring.

takeaways.technique: Per-ticket acceptance as the payment/credit trigger
takeaways.what_they_do: Each ticket is graded in story points at architecture time; the engineer is paid only when the ticket is accepted, after internal QA rounds and client sign-off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when that ticket is accepted, the engineer gets paid a a fee per story point that they complete

takeaways.what_they_do: Strategists who scope the work are paid on a different metric (customer happiness/NPS) than the engineers who execute, so scoping inflation is checked by someone with opposite incentives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: strategists are compensated based on NR which really is like customer happiness

takeaways.what_they_do: Every ticket passes multiple internal QA rounds involving the strategist, then client approval, before payment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single ticket has to be approved internally with multiple rounds of QA

takeaways.technique: Hiring bar as the quality lever
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately make hiring hard so process can stay light; the claim is AI amplifies existing skill, good or bad.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI makes people look like one of those crazy mirrors where any one of your attributes, it makes it 10 times larger
